tasks.name: Create Logger Interface and Implementation
tasks.description: Implement logging interface as Protocol for dependency injection and structured output throughout the application. Create logger package with abstract Protocol definition and console implementation.
tasks.notes: Logger Protocol enables testing with mock implementations. ConsoleLogger provides immediate working implementation. Color output optional but preferred for better UX. Summary formatting should be human-readable with counts and processing time.

relatedFiles.description: Add Logger and ConsoleLogger to exports

tasks.implementationGuide:
1. Create src/interfaces/ directory with __init__.py package initialization
2. Create src/interfaces/logger.py with Logger Protocol defining methods: info(message: str), debug(message: str), error(message: str), log_summary(summary: dict)
3. Create src/loggers/ directory with __init__.py
4. Implement src/loggers/console_logger.py with ConsoleLogger class implementing Logger Protocol
5. ConsoleLogger should handle verbose flag in constructor: ConsoleLogger(verbose: bool = False)
6. info() prints to stdout, error() prints to stderr with color if available
7. debug() only prints if verbose=True
8. log_summary() formats and displays structured summary data
9. Update src/__init__.py to export Logger protocol and ConsoleLogger
10. Follow established patterns: Protocol for interface, concrete implementation with dependency injection via constructor
tasks.verificationCriteria: Logger Protocol defines consistent interface with info/debug/error/log_summary methods. ConsoleLogger implements Protocol correctly with verbose handling. Both Logger and ConsoleLogger importable from src package. Code follows UP035 rule and existing naming conventions.

tasks.name: Implement MigrationCoordinator Orchestration Class
tasks.description: Create MigrationCoordinator class in coordinators package to orchestrate complete migration workflow. Handles cursor-based pagination, data transformation, persistence, and error management while maintaining single responsibility principle.
tasks.notes: MigrationCoordinator orchestrates without implementing business logic - delegates to injected dependencies. Cursor pagination follows GraphQL Connection specification from existing queries. Error handling preserves domain exceptions while logging details. Private methods enable reuse and testing.

relatedFiles.description: Add MigrationCoordinator to main package exports
Reference for GraphQL response structure and pagination
Reference for entity mapping method signatures

tasks.implementationGuide:
1. Create src/coordinators/ directory with __init__.py package initialization
2. Create src/coordinators/migration_coordinator.py with MigrationCoordinator class
3. Constructor requires dependencies: MigrationCoordinator(jobber_client: JobberClient, entity_mapper: EntityMapper, repository: Repository, logger: Logger)
4. Implement migrate() -> MigrationSummary method as main workflow orchestration:
   - Initialize database schema via repository.init_schema()
   - Create MigrationSummary with start time
   - Call _migrate_clients() for cursor pagination loop
   - Call _migrate_invoices() for cursor pagination loop  
   - Calculate duration and return summary
5. Implement _migrate_clients() -> int private method:
   - Cursor pagination loop until hasNextPage=False
   - Extract edges/nodes from GraphQL response
   - Map each client via entity_mapper.map_client()
   - Batch save via repository.save_clients()
   - Log progress and return total count
6. Implement _migrate_invoices() -> int private method: Similar to clients but for invoices
7. Add comprehensive error handling with domain exceptions
8. Update src/coordinators/__init__.py to export MigrationCoordinator
9. Update src/__init__.py to include MigrationCoordinator

tasks.name: Implement Typer-based CLI with Dependency Injection
tasks.description: Create CLI module using Typer framework to provide command-line interface with migrate subcommand. Implements dependency injection container pattern to wire all components and provides user-friendly interface matching shrimp-rules.md specifications.
tasks.notes: CLI follows factory pattern for dependency injection. Error handling provides user-friendly messages while preserving technical details for debugging. Database connection properly managed with cleanup. Exit codes enable script integration and monitoring.

relatedFiles.description: Main CLI module with Typer application and dependency injection
Reference for CLI entry point configuration
Reference for CLI requirements and specifications

tasks.implementationGuide:
1. Create src/cli.py as main CLI module
2. Import required components: typer, Path, sqlite3, all domain classes
3. Create typer.Typer() app instance with help text: "TightBeam v2 - Jobber Data Migration Tool"
4. Implement migrate command with signature:
   @app.command()
   def migrate(db: Path = typer.Option(..., help="SQLite database path"), verbose: bool = typer.Option(False, "-v", help="Enable verbose logging"))
5. Implement dependency injection in migrate():
   - Create sqlite3.Connection from db path
   - Instantiate AuthProvider()
   - Create JobberClient(auth_provider)
   - Create EntityMapper()
   - Create Repository(connection)
   - Create ConsoleLogger(verbose)
   - Create MigrationCoordinator with all dependencies
6. Add comprehensive error handling:
   - Catch domain exceptions and display user-friendly messages
   - Use appropriate exit codes: 0=success, 1=config, 2=api, 3=mapping, 4=repository
   - Close database connection in finally block
7. Implement main() function as entry point that calls app()
8. Add if __name__ == "__main__": main() for direct execution
tasks.verificationCriteria: CLI provides migrate command with required --db option and optional --verbose flag. Dependency injection creates all components correctly with proper error handling. User-friendly error messages with appropriate exit codes. Database connection managed properly with cleanup. Entry point works with Poetry configuration.
